_metadata.fpl_basis_note: PTC for coverage year 2026 uses the poverty guidelines most recently published as of the first day of open enrollment (November 1, 2025): the 2025 guidelines (26 CFR 1.36B-1(h)).
_metadata.source: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-25 (applicable percentage table and required contribution percentage for 2026); Public Law 119-21 sections 71302, 71304, 71305 as implemented in IRS FS-2025-10, IR-2025-127 and the proposed regulations at 91 FR 65494
_metadata.verification_note: Applicable percentage table scraped in full from Rev. Proc. 2025-25 (posted to issue #18, pass 3); PL 119-21 effective dates quoted from 91 FR 65494 (issue #18, pass 4). No law extended the ARPA/IRA enhanced credits for 2026 (H.R.5145 introduced only).

pl_119_21.71302: Removes 36B(c)(1)(B) for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025: a lawfully present noncitizen below 100% FPL who is ineligible for Medicaid because of immigration status is no longer an applicable taxpayer.
pl_119_21.71304: For plan years beginning after December 31, 2025, a plan enrolled in during a special enrollment period based on a change in expected household income is not a qualified health plan for the PTC.
pl_119_21.71305: Removes the 36B(f)(2)(B) repayment limitation for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025: excess advance PTC is repaid in full.
pl_119_21.71301_not_in_2026: Eligible-alien restriction applies to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2026.
pl_119_21.71303_not_in_2026: Pre-enrollment verification applies to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027.

notes: The ARPA/IRA enhanced credits (no 400% FPL limit, 0-8.5% contribution) applied to 2021-2025 only.
Rows give the applicable percentage at the start (initial) and end (final) of each band; within a band it rises linearly (26 CFR 1.36B-3(g)).
The first band is 'less than 133%' and the last is 'at least 300% but not more than 400%'.
